title: Paid in Engine Parts

beats.text: The best stock deal in car history was paid in engine parts.
Detroit, nineteen oh three. Henry Ford can't pay your bill.
So your ten thousand dollars of parts buys ten percent of his company.
The Model T takes off. Dividends pour in by the million.
In nineteen sixteen, Henry stops the big dividends to build cheaper cars.
Can a boss just keep the owners' profits?
You see, you co-own a pizzeria, and your partner keeps every slice for a bigger oven.
In nineteen nineteen, Michigan's top court says a company exists mainly for its stockholders' profit.
Ford pays out nineteen million dollars.
So Henry plans a new company with a cheaper car.
Everyone else sells, and Henry buys every last share.
Your ten thousand dollars of parts becomes twenty-five million.
Henry lost the case, and won the whole company.

facts.claim: In 1903 John and Horace Dodge (Dodge Brothers machine shop, Detroit) supplied the mechanical parts of the first Ford car and received 10% of Ford Motor Company (50 shares each of 1,000) for $10,000 in materials/credit; Ford could not pay them fully in cash
Ford dividends to shareholders ran into the millions (special dividends of $34 million in 1914-15; the Dodges took about $5.4 million in dividends overall)

In 1916 Henry Ford ended/slashed special dividends, saying he wanted to put profits back into the business, employ more men and keep cutting car prices (and build the River Rouge plant); the Dodges sued in 1916

In 1919 the Michigan Supreme Court held 'A business corporation is organized and carried on primarily for the profit of the stockholders' and upheld an extra dividend of about $19.3 million ($19,275,385)

In March 1919 Henry Ford announced a plan for a new company to build cars cheaper than the Model T (threatened a competing manufacturer); by July 1919 he had bought out all seven minority stockholders, giving the Fords sole ownership
The Dodges sold their Ford stock to Henry Ford in 1919 for $25 million

caption:
1903: Henry Ford couldn't pay the Dodge brothers' bill, so $10,000 of parts became 10% of Ford.
In 1916 he stopped the big dividends. They sued, and in 1919 the court said a company is run mainly for its stockholders.
Then Henry bought every share. The Dodges' stake: $25 million.
